items.bewering: Sjokolade begin as die bone binne die dik vrug van 'n kakaoboom.
items.bron: ICCO, 'Harvesting & Post-harvest' (icco.org/harvesting-post-harvest-new/): beans are taken from the split pod and processed into chocolate; IFT 'How dark chocolate is processed' (ift.org).

items.bewering: Kakaobome het warm en nat plekke naby die ekwator nodig om te groei.
items.bron: Several sources agree cacao grows only within about 20 degrees of the equator, mostly within 10 degrees, needing 20-30 C, high rainfall and humidity, and does not tolerate drought (e.g. hunker.com climate summary; Lyon, 'Cacao Culture in the Philippines', Project Gutenberg). Consistent with ICCO producer lists, which are all tropical countries.

items.bewering: Die grootste deel van die wêreld se kakao groei in Afrika, veral in Ivoorkus en Ghana.
items.bron: ICCO Quarterly Bulletin of Cocoa Statistics production tables (icco.org, QBCS XLIV No. 3 and XLV No. 4): Africa 73-77% of world output, Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana the two largest producers. UNCTAD (unctad.org/node/13076): Côte d'Ivoire 40-45% of world beans. More recent ICCO-cited estimates (2024/25) still put Africa near 69%, so 'die grootste deel' holds even in a weak year.

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika het nie sulke plekke nie, en ons kakao kom van ver af.
items.bron: South Africa's northernmost town, Musina, lies at about 22.4 S (latitude.to; Limpopo is the northernmost province, Wikipedia 'Limpopo'), outside the roughly 20-degree cacao belt. Tridge market overview classes South Africa as an import-dependent net importer of cocoa beans; Food For Mzansi (foodformzansi.co.za, 'Rising cocoa prices hit South Africa hard') says local chocolate makers depend on imported beans. One Statista market overview mentions local cocoa growing in passing, but it is boilerplate market copy with no figures; no commercial South African production appears in ICCO producer lists.

items.bewering: Die boer sny die ryp kakaopeul van die boom en haal die nat bone uit.
items.bron: ICCO, 'Harvesting & Post-harvest': ripe pods are cut from the tree with a sharp blade or pruning hook, split, and the wet beans pulled out by hand.

items.bewering: Vars bone smaak bitter en nog nie na sjokolade nie.
items.bron: TNAU Agritech post-harvest page on cocoa (agritech.tnau.ac.in): fermentation is needed to develop flavour precursors and reduce bitterness; growables.org 'The science of cacao fermentation': raw beans are astringent and unpleasant and must be fermented, dried and roasted before they taste like chocolate.

items.bewering: Die boer gooi hulle op 'n hoop en laat hulle 'n paar dae lank gis.
items.bron: ICCO, 'Harvesting & Post-harvest': beans are piled in heaps (or boxes) under banana leaves; fermentation lasts about 5 days for Forastero and 2-3 days for Criollo. TNAU: standard heap method about six days.

items.bewering: 'n Groot deel van die sjokolade se smaak kom uit daardie gisting.
items.bron: ICCO, 'Harvesting & Post-harvest': during fermentation enzyme activity, oxidation and protein breakdown develop the chocolate flavour and colour; TNAU: fermentation develops flavour and aroma precursors. 'n Groot deel' (not 'all') is the right strength, since roasting also develops flavour.

items.bewering: Daarna droog die bone in die son, en hulle word meer werd.
items.bron: ICCO, 'Harvesting & Post-harvest': beans are dried from about 60% to 7.5% moisture, by sun or in dryers, and then bagged for delivery; dried fermented beans are the traded commodity, so the step adds value (value-chain framing in Cocoa Barometer 2015, oxfamnovib.nl).

items.bewering: Sakke droë bone gaan per vragmotor na die hawe en per skip weg.
items.bron: MSC Ivory Coast cocoa page (msc.com): inland trucking to port and San Pedro as the world's leading cocoa export port; Bloomberg, 5 Dec 2025: Abidjan and San Pedro clogged with truckloads of cocoa; Reuters archive 2011: sacks loaded onto ships at Abidjan. (Some beans now also ship in bulk, which does not make the sentence false.)

items.bewering: In die fabriek rooster masjiene die bone en breek hul harde doppe af.
items.bron: IFT, 'How dark chocolate is processed': roasting, then a winnowing machine cracks the shells and blows them away, leaving nibs. Whitaker's and Food Research Lab: husks are hard, brittle and inedible, and roasting makes them brittle. Some makers roast the nibs after winnowing, but bean roasting first is the common order.

items.bewering: Ander masjiene maal die stukkies fyn totdat hulle dik en vloeibaar word.
items.bron: OSU bulk commodity chain project, 'Roasting, Winnowing, and Grinding' (u.osu.edu): grinding produces heat from friction and gives chocolate liquor, nib particles suspended in cocoa butter; ICCO 'Processing Cocoa' describes hot cocoa liquor.

items.bewering: Die fabriek meng suiker en dikwels ook melk daarby.
items.bron: OSU bulk commodity chain project: for milk chocolate, liquor and cocoa butter are blended with sugar, milk and vanilla. 'Dikwels' is right, since dark chocolate has no milk.

items.bewering: Die mengsel word in vorms gegiet, en so word dit blokke.
items.bron: Britannica, 'How Is Chocolate Made?'; Hill Country Chocolate guide: after conching and tempering, the chocolate is poured into moulds and cooled. The lesson leaves out conching and tempering, which is a simplification and not a false statement.

items.bewering: Die gerooste en gemaalde bone is weer meer werd.
items.bron: Cocoa Barometer 2015 (oxfamnovib.nl): processing and manufacturing take a much larger share of a bar's value than the farmer's beans; ICCO/UNCTAD 2016 presentation on the concentrated processing step.

items.bewering: Vragmotors neem die toegedraaide blokke na winkels in baie lande.
items.bron: CBI market information on cocoa and chocolate (cbi.eu); Trend Economy 2023 data show chocolate traded into South Africa from Belgium, Italy and Germany, so finished bars cross borders to shops in many countries.

items.bewering: Sulke fabrieke staan gewoonlik ver van die plase waar die hulpbron groei.
items.bron: ICCO grindings bulletins (QBCS L/LI): Europe is the largest grinding region (about 35%), with the Netherlands and Germany biggest; Fitch Solutions via MyJoyOnline: West African output sits upstream with most value added in Europe; CBI: limited room for value addition in producing countries. Note for the record: grinding into cocoa liquor and butter does happen at origin on a large scale (Côte d'Ivoire is among the world's biggest grinders), but finished chocolate making, the sugar-milk-moulding stage this block describes, is concentrated in consuming countries. 'Gewoonlik' carries that.

items.bewering: Al die maakwerk in die fabriek saam noem ons die vervaardigingsproses.
items.blok: Die waarde klim by elke stap
items.bron: TWI Global, 'What is manufacturing?' (twi-global.com) and Kalkine Media's definition: manufacturing is turning raw materials into finished goods with machinery, labour and processing; the factory steps in the IFT and Britannica process descriptions are exactly that.

items.bewering: Elke stap op die plaas en in die fabriek voeg iets by die bone se waarde. (Kop: 'Die waarde klim by elke stap')
items.blok: Die waarde klim by elke stap
items.bron: Cocoa Barometer 2015 and FAO/BASIC 2020 'Comparative study on the distribution of value in European chocolate chains' (cocoainitiative.org): value builds up cumulatively along the chain. The 'climbing' picture maps correctly: value adds on and does not fall back between the steps the lesson names.

items.bewering: Die toegedraaide blok op die winkel se rak is die meeste werd.
items.blok: Die waarde klim by elke stap
items.bron: Cocoa Barometer 2015: the retail price of the finished bar is the full value that is split along the chain (farmer 6.6%, manufacturers 35.2%, retail and taxes 44.2%), so the bar on the shelf is the highest-value form.

items.bewering: Lys van koste langs die pad: die boer se werk en gereedskap; die dae wat die bone gis en droog; vervoer na die hawe; die skip oor die see; die fabriek se masjiene en krag; die lone van die fabriek se werkers; die papier om die blokke toe te draai; die winkel se huur en ligte.
items.blok: Wat dit langs die pad kos
items.bron: Each item matches a stage in the ICCO post-harvest and processing descriptions and the MSC logistics page; fermentation and drying take days of labour and space (ICCO), and the retail costs are ordinary retail overheads. Read as a set, the list follows the same order as the lesson's own steps.

items.bewering: Die boer, die fabriek en die winkel kry elkeen geld vir wat hulle verkoop. Uit daardie geld betaal elkeen eers al sy koste. Sy wins is die geld wat daarna oorbly.
items.blok: Waar die wins die opvallendste is
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'profit': money made in a business after all the costs and expenses are paid; Vocabulary.com: the amount by which revenue exceeds cost. The chain is simplified: traders, exporters, grinders and shippers are left out, and in the Cocoa Barometer they take part of the roughly 14% not shown in the farmer, manufacturer and retail shares. Nothing here says only these three are paid, so this is not false.

items.bewering: Die boer verkoop sy bone voordat die meeste waarde bygevoeg word.
items.blok: Waar die wins die opvallendste is
items.bron: Cocoa Barometer 2015: the farmer receives about 6.6% of a bar's value, and the rest is added downstream.

items.bewering: Die grootste deel van 'n blok se waarde beland daarom nie by die boer nie.
items.blok: Waar die wins die opvallendste is
items.bron: Cocoa Barometer 2015 (farmer 6.6%); FAO/BASIC 2020 (cocoa-producing countries as a whole capture about 18.6% of value in the French chain).

items.bewering: Die meeste daarvan word by die fabriek en die winkel bygevoeg, ver van die plaas.
items.blok: Waar die wins die opvallendste is
items.bron: Cocoa Barometer 2015: manufacturers 35.2% plus retail and taxes 44.2%, about 79% together; FAO/BASIC 2020: brands and retailers capture about 70% of total value. Both are largely in consuming countries (see the factory-location item).

items.bewering: Daar is die wins gewoonlik die opvallendste. (Ook die kop: 'Waar die wins die opvallendste is')
items.blok: Waar die wins die opvallendste is
items.bron: FAO/BASIC 2020 value-distribution study and Cocoa Barometer 2015: value and margins concentrate with chocolate brands and retailers, while farm incomes are very low. 'Opvallendste' plus 'gewoonlik' is a hedged, relative claim and the sources support it. The studies measure share of value rather than net profit, and the lesson does not claim a precise profit figure.

items.bewering: Hoeveel wins elkeen maak, wissel van jaar tot jaar en van blok tot blok.
items.blok: Waar die wins die opvallendste is
items.bron: Food For Mzansi on the recent cocoa price surge hitting South African makers; Bloomberg, Dec 2025, on falling prices and an exporter cash crunch; the Cocoa Barometer figures are tied to one bar price and year. Shares and margins clearly move with bean prices and product.

items.bewering: kakao: Die bone van die kakaoboom, waarvan mense sjokolade maak.
items.bron: ICCO and IFT process descriptions: chocolate is made from the fermented, dried and roasted seeds (beans) of Theobroma cacao. 'Kakao' also names the powder and the tree, but the narrower sense defined here is a correct sense.

items.bewering: kakaopeul: Die dik vrug van 'n kakaoboom, met bone binne-in.
items.bron: ICCO, 'Harvesting & Post-harvest': the pod has to be struck with a club or machete to split it, and the wet beans lie inside.

items.bewering: gisting: Die proses waarin klein lewende dinge kos of sap verander.
items.bron: ICCO, 'Harvesting & Post-harvest': in cocoa fermentation micro-organisms (yeasts, then bacteria) turn the pulp sugars into ethanol and then acetic acid. 'Klein lewende dinge' is a fair Grade 6 rendering of micro-organisms. In cocoa the flavour change inside the bean is driven by the bean's own enzymes, set off by the microbes' heat and acid, which the definition does not contradict.

items.bewering: vervaardigingsproses: Die stappe waarmee mense van grondstowwe of ander goedere iets nuuts maak.
items.bron: TWI Global, 'What is manufacturing?' (twi-global.com): manufacturing is transforming raw materials into finished goods; Kalkine Media: turning raw materials into finished goods with machinery, labour and processing. Including 'ander goedere' (components) is consistent with standard usage.

items.bewering: wins: Wins is die geld wat oorbly nadat iemand al sy koste uit sy verkoopprys betaal het.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'profit' (britannica.com/dictionary/profit): money made after all the costs and expenses are paid. Consistent with the study block's own wording.

opsomming: Every checkable claim held up against ICCO, Cocoa Barometer, FAO/BASIC and process sources, so nothing contradicted and nothing uncertain; the closest call is that factories sit 'gewoonlik ver' from farms, which is true of finished chocolate making even though a lot of bean grinding now happens in Côte d'Ivoire, and the lesson's 'gewoonlik' carries that; there is no analogy beyond 'die waarde klim', whose mapping holds.
